title: Home
note: Opens with a one-line briefing, then the two tasks that matter most, each with its button on the card. Balances and the clock are glanceable tiles.

title: Ask Kithena
note: A small card anchored above the tab bar, never full screen. Answers end in the action itself, so a question becomes a request in one tap.

title: The People tab, all of it
note: No menu of sections. One scroll: search that understands questions, what needs you (Review, decided in place), who is starting, two headline numbers, then the directory. Shown at full scroll length.

title: Review, opened in place
note: “Show all 11” grows the card instead of opening a new page. Simple decisions are a tick or a cross on the row; anything with a flag opens a modal.

title: Deciding a flagged change
note: A centred modal with the before and after, and why Kithena flagged it in plain words.

title: Search that answers
note: The same box takes names or questions. The answer shows the people and the next sensible action; the chips show how the question was read, and each can be removed.

title: Filters
note: Chips with live counts in a centred modal. The button says how many people you’ll get.

title: Org chart, same place
note: List and Org chart are a toggle on the directory, not separate pages. The tree folds; tapping a person opens their profile.

title: Everything else, one tap away
note: The less frequent HR jobs live in one menu on the title bar, so the tab itself stays a single list. Each opens a modal.

title: Import
note: Drop a spreadsheet; Kithena maps the columns and asks only about the one it isn’t sure of. Nothing is written until Import.

title: Export
note: Three questions and a reason. Sensitive fields need an extra approval, said up front.

title: Insights
note: A summary sentence first, then four numbers and one chart. Scheduled reports sit at the bottom of the same page.

title: A profile, as HR
note: A photo header with four quick actions, then the four facts people look for most. Below, every detail is a row with an icon, a small grey label and a large value, so the answer is what the eye lands on.

title: The rest of the record
note: Scrolling on from P11: one card per section, no pills to switch. Missing details say “Not added yet” with an Ask button; pending changes sit under the value they’ll replace; sensitive values stay masked until the eye is tapped.

title: Me
note: Your own record uses the same layout as everyone else’s, opening with what HR still needs. Settings is in the Me tab.

title: Changing a detail
note: Edits are one modal per section, never a separate page. When a change needs approval, the modal says who and what happens meanwhile.

title: Fixing a refused value
note: Kithena works out the right check letter and offers it as one tap. Scanning the card is the fallback.

title: Profile actions
note: One menu for every move HR can make. Each item opens a centred modal.

title: Someone is leaving
note: Two fields, then everything Kithena will do because of them, so nothing is forgotten and nothing is a surprise.

title: History
note: Before and after on every line. “As it was on…” rebuilds the whole record for any date.

title: Add a person
note: Five fields in a modal, or drop the offer letter and check what Kithena filled in.

title: A new starter’s first steps
note: One checklist; the current step opens in place. Kithena checks the IBAN as it’s typed and names the bank.

title: The Time off tab, all of it
note: Clock, balance, a box to describe what you want, what’s coming up, who’s off this week, the bigger plans and holidays: one scroll, no sub-pages. Shown at full scroll length.

title: Describe it
note: Type it the way you’d say it. Kithena shows how it read it, the result in plain words, and one smarter option. Send is pinned in thumb reach.

title: Request with a calendar
note: For people who’d rather tap: type, dates and the result in one centred modal. Weekends and holidays aren’t counted.

title: Change or cancel
note: Tap any upcoming request. Each option says what happens to your balance before you choose.

title: A missed clock-out
note: Kithena suggests the likely time from signals it already has, and says which ones. One tap, then Marco confirms.

title: Where the days went
note: Tap Details on the balance. A plain ledger, in a modal.

title: Tap a day
note: Each day in “Team this week” opens who’s out and why.

title: As a manager
note: Approvals sit on the Time off tab as well as the Inbox, each with the one fact that matters. Approve is on the card.

title: Solving a clash
note: “Options” opens choices with their cost spelled out, instead of a bare decline.

title: Planning parental leave
note: The one long flow that earns its own screen. Kithena drafts the whole plan and the handover; you change what you want.

title: The Inbox tab, all of it
note: To do and Updates in one scroll, under a one-line summary. Every task has its button on the card, so most are finished without opening anything. The chips are the four lanes: To do, Updates, My requests and Done. Shown at full scroll length.

title: A task, done in a modal
note: Add opens a centred modal with the form and a suggestion from your contacts. Saving closes it and the card leaves To do.

title: Signing
note: The document, a three-line summary of what changes, and a typed signature. All in one modal.

title: Tidying an update
note: Long-press any update for a small menu. Tasks can’t be muted; only updates can.

title: As a manager
note: Approve straight from the card. People’s Review queue appears as one bundled task, so nothing is counted twice.

title: Handing over
note: Who, when and what, in one modal. Kithena says why the suggested person fits.

title: My requests
note: Who has each thing you asked for, and since when. Nudge appears once a request has waited a day.

title: Done
note: Everything finished, with its outcome, grouped by month and searchable.

title: Nothing to do
note: A calm empty state with the next thing worth knowing.

title: As HR
note: Shared tasks show whether anyone has taken them. Kithena names the likely cause on the card.

title: Every setting, one list
note: All of People, Time off and your own settings on one list, each row with a one-line summary of how it’s set now. The search box also takes plain requests. Shown at full scroll length.

title: Change a setting by asking
note: Say what you want. Kithena finds the setting, shows the before and after and who it affects, and saves it as a draft.

title: Employee fields
note: Each field reads as one sentence: who fills it in and who sees it. Sections are chips; a new field can be described in words.

title: Editing a field
note: The four-step wizard becomes one sentence. Each highlighted part is a choice; the preview and the rarer options sit underneath.

title: Changing one part
note: Tapping a part opens a short menu right under it. The sentence rewrites itself as you tick.

title: A new field, described
note: Describe it; Kithena drafts the name, answer type and access. You check one sentence, not a form.

title: Organisation
note: Entities, locations and the three company-wide rules, each as a readable row.

title: Roles
note: Four cards: what each role can do in one line, who has it, and one button.

title: Integrations
note: One page instead of four tabs: the connection, what goes to chat as two short lists of switches, then identity and webhooks.

title: Activity log
note: Who changed what, with the before and after in one line.

title: Leave types
note: Each kind of leave in one plain line: how much, and who approves. Creating one starts with describing it.

title: A leave type, described
note: Paste the handbook line or say it. Kithena drafts the rules and asks the one question the text leaves open.

title: One leave type
note: Six rules, each a label and a plain answer. Tap a row to change it in a modal; Preview shows the balance as one employee would see it.

title: Holidays
note: Per location, kept up to date from official calendars. Company days off are added on top.

title: Approvals
note: Three short lists: who approves what, how many must stay in, and what happens when nobody answers.

title: Attendance
note: Switches for how people clock in, and three rows for what counts as a working day.

title: Balance rules
note: The rule, and an example with a real person’s numbers so its effect is obvious.

title: Notifications
note: Tasks are always delivered; updates can be muted by kind. Quiet hours hold both, except tasks due today.
